title: Latent-Guided Cooperative Energy-Based Models
claim: Learned representations from the baseline mix semantic classes, while adding latent guidance yields clearly separated, well-structured class clusters.
layout: 3 scatter panels side by side, left-to-right, shared class legend at right
description: A single row of three t-SNE scatter plots in bordered boxes, with a shared legend for classes 0 to 9 at the far right. Each point is a CIFAR-10 sample, colored by class. The left plot is a diffuse blob where colors overlap heavily, with no visible class structure. The middle plot shows partial clustering, with some groups such as orange, cyan and olive emerging, but with a muddy, mixed center. The right plot shows compact, distinct, well-separated color clusters arranged radially. The eye goes to the right panel, which is the cleanest. The panels have no titles in the crop, so the progression from mixed to separated is communicated by the point colors alone.
caption: t-SNE visualization trained on CIFAR-10: cooperative EBM with F (fϕ(x)) as energy function vs. our LGCEBM.
abstract: Energy-based models (EBMs) provide a flexible framework for generative models with strong distribution modeling capabilities. Nevertheless, their broader adoption has been limited by the difficulty of stable and efficient training. In this paper, we propose a unified and efficient latent-guided cooperative EBM that leverages informative target latent variables to guide the joint energy in capturing both data distribution and semantic structure, along with a cooperative generator designed for effective MCMC initialization. Our joint space optimization only requires MCMC sampling in the data space, and allows the energy to learn semantic data–latent relationships directly from real data. Experiments show our method improves generation quality and training stability with fewer resources, and performs effectively across multiple downstream tasks.
